newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish firms Aug earnings continue slight uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Polish firms Aug earnings continue slight uptrend.

text.p: Firms listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange recorded slightly better earnings in August for the second month in a row, a tendency that could help keep the bourse mood positive, analysts said on Thursday.
But they said investors would best wait for the earnings rally to continue to the end of the year.

"The August results are a continuation of last month since they're better than the first half, which could mean the start of a trend, but it's hard to say what will happen by the end of the year," said Pawel Hominski of Magnus brokerage.

Analysts had said uninspiring May and June earnings had hastened July's downward correction that followed the bourse's 90-percent surge this year. Weaker earnings over the first four months had been blamed partly on this year's harsh winter.
Analysts said there was always the danger that auditors would pare preliminary profit reports, as happened with three main-market firms for 1995 earlier this year.
"There could still be many nasty surprises," said Jacek Dzierwa, Polish Equity Analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
But Dzierwa said the bourse could rise by at least another 10 percent this year, helped by better earnings and especially by the arrival of capital from foreign investment funds.
Firms showing good results tended to rise on the bourse on Thursday, such as the two top gainers, furniture maker Forte and paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn.
Thursday's biggers losers Espebepe and Remak plunged by or near the maximum 10 percent after publishing weak August earnings.
Analysts liked Cieszyn and rival paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw in the longer term, though said Wroclaw looked cheaper at the moment and warned that the fourth quarter was a tough time for the industry.

Analysts also favoured banks, which continued to show good results, and tyremakers Debica and Stomil Olsztyn, though Stomil was cheaper especially after its 9.1-percent plunge on Thursday after its lower August profit.
Debica recorded its highest monthly net profit in August but did so on financial rather than operational gains.
Analyts said that among sectors containing small-cap stocks, textile firms were seen rebounding upon a better business cycle in Germany, but meat firms could be stung by higher fodder prices.
